bga_name: The Fox in the Forest: Duet
rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Round End 4 Game End Overview This is a co-operative version of the also two player Fox in the Forest (competitive) Gather all the gems before time runs out Turn A round consists of 11 turns Each turn, one player will lead the trick and the other will follow The player who won the most recent trick, leads the current trick The leader plays any card from their hand The follower must play a card matching the suit of the leader's, or play any card if they do not hold that suit The Decree card, which was revealed in setup and can be changed during the game, shows the Trump suit i.e. the suit that beats the lead suit If you played a card with an Odd number, enact its ability when appropriate The winner of the trick is either the player who played the highest Trump, or if none were played then the winner is the player who played the highest lead suit After the winner is determined, you will find paw prints on the two played cards, these combined determine how far the movement piece moves towards the trick winner e.g. a 2 paws and 3 paws would cause 5 movement in the winner's direction If when moving the team tracker it would move off the board on either end, move it back to the central space and cover the last visible space on the end which was moved off from with a forest marker e.g. if the movement made the piece leave the board on the right, the first available space from the right edge of the board would receive forest, this therefore permanently shortens the path for the rest of the game. If the Forest marker would go on an unclaimed gem space, move the gem closer along into the next accessible space on the path. If after moving step, the team tracker is on a space connected to Gems without a reset, you may claim a single gem from that pile regardless of how many may be stacked there (even if the tracker did not move) After a Trick is resolved, place the played cards nearby so it is easily accessible for reference during future tricks, then start a new trick with the winner of the current one Round End The round ends after 11 tricks, at which point perform the following: Add a gem to each space which contains a + Add a Forest token to one end of the path, the players may choose the end except when the team tracker is on the last space of one end then they have to choose the other. If there are no Forest tokens left to place, continue the game without placing a token. As with during the game, if placing the new Forest token covers an occupied gem space, move the gems one space inwards Shuffle all 30 cards and deal out 11 each in addition to revealing a single card for the start Decree The Team Tracker remains in the space it ended the round it, it does NOT reset to the central space Game End If the players have to place a Forest token when there are no tokens left, they LOSE! If the players have taken 3 rounds and still haven't succeeded, they LOSE! If the players collect all the gems before the end of the 3rd round, they Win! IF the players Win, they may score as follows: Score 10, 20, or 30 points depending on whether you chose a Level 1 game, a Level 2 game, or a Level 3 game (higher the level, higher the difficulty) Score 1 point for each remaining hand card Score 10 points if you won in round 2 Score 3 points for each unplaced Forest token

---

community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] Not the games fault, but I missed that this game was a cooperative game.   We simply don't really like coops and the game feels a bit "bland" and "too simplistic" for us.  We played it once and had no problem to clear the "base" board, and we had quite a few turns "left" before the game would have ended.  Difficulty is not really that hard and the puzzle of the game also does not really grab me as much as I might have liked.  We will likely not play it very often in the future.

[Rating: 3/10] This game has an interesting premise, but making players be silent during the game takes away a lot of the interaction I look for in games.

[Rating: 3/10] Sadly, this game didn't do it for me. As much as I liked the original and as much as I like cooperative games, the addition of the paws on the cards felt too fiddly/arbitrary. The idea of trick taking is playing the powerful cards at the right time, and keeping track of the important cards, but the relation between card strength and paws is just non-existent, which means it ends up being a chore to get the right number of paws at the right time.

[Rating: 3/10] Fox and the Forest Duet is a bit narrow- you have to accomplish specific things which is not a way we really enjoyed playing a trick taking game. Sky Team is a different way to play coop and have narrow requirements that we have really enjoyed.

[Rating: 3/10] Like the The Fox in the Forest base game, I wanted better art, better theming, more story, and a deeper game. Way too much to ask for a  game that's just a glorified trick taking game.  I wanted more, but I also don't like trick taking games.  If you play with someone who knows the game well, you're almost guaranteed to win. Feels too easy when your partner knows math / stats. You can essentially be carried. Game doesn't work if there's too much table talk too.

[Rating: 3/10] My first and only trick taking game. Very boring, couldnt get through it, if you like simple card games then yer but has such low content and is just bad

[Rating: 3.5/10] Not as good as original Fox in the Forest. Cooperative element doesn't work well and they removed the competitive challenge that kept us engaged. Also theme does not make sense - why are there gems in a forest? Why is the forest shrinking?

[Rating: 4/10] Pretty disappointed with this game after how much I loved both The Fox in the Forest (2 player trick-taking) and The Crew (cooperative trick-taking). This just fell kinda flat, and wasn't very hard.  Beautiful art and presentation though.

[Rating: 4/10] Simply not a fan of co-operative games, but gave it a go with hope but simply couldn't warm to it. Some instructions are somewhat woolly. More a fan of the competitive version.
